# Additional Task2 review: fractional chapter boundary precision

Reviewer scope: read-only diagnosis of the controller's new actual-narration
failure, followed by this explicitly requested review note. No product edits,
index/HEAD changes, test suites, subagents, or repeated acceptance runs.

## Important finding

`skills/teacher/skills/explorable/scripts/bundle_templates.mjs:62` assigns the
full-precision scene start to `video.currentTime` when a chapter is clicked,
but `current()` resolves a scene using strict `s.start <= video.currentTime`.
Explore immediately pauses the video and transfers `scenes[current()]`.

The new fixture's chapter 5 starts at `53.15591666666667`. A focused real-browser
probe found that assigning that value returns `53.155916` immediately and after
the seek completes. The paused media time remains about 0.667 microseconds
before the unquantized chapter boundary, so the strict resolver selects scene 4.
Waiting for `seeked` alone does not resolve this state.

This mechanism explains both original-check failures in
`.superpowers/sdd/RESUME-20261024/fresh-confirmation-matching-timing/command.json`:

```text
Error: [{"name":"interactive video chapter and paused model transfer","ok":false},{"name":"explorer receives scene parameters","ok":false}]
```

That controller run has returncode 1, duration 6.189836958001251 seconds, and
recorded PID events `max 0` through playback/exploration. Its pinned runtime is
the unchanged image
`sha256:96e50ad889f7fb38c3360c76c7908d3a9b6b26ec590b82cc316993d6eeae520f`.
Its exact returned media time was not instrumented by this reviewer.

This is an Important runtime defect that blocks full acceptance. It is a
pre-existing chapter-resolution issue exposed by new timing; the reviewed
caption correction did not introduce the strict scene comparison. The failure
does not establish a regression in the source-backed browser-pool repair.

## Actual focused probe

Executed from
`/Users/prax/Developer/skills-and-personas-recovery-20261016/.worktrees/teach-finish-20261024`.
This used the provisioned host browser, Chromium `153.0.8010.12`, with the
reviewed original real MP4. It was a precision discrimination probe, not a
pinned-container acceptance run or a new narrated fixture. The page/media
existed only in the launched browser; no source or probe file was created.
